observations: Figure 3. (a) Hierarchical Cluster of Countries based on average marginal causal effect. One hundred thirty countries with at least 100 respondents are selected. Three colors of the dendrogram branches represent three clusters -- Western, Eastern, and Southern. Names of the countries are colored according to Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map 2010-2014*. Distributions across three clusters reveal stark differences. For instance, cluster 2 (Eastern) mostly consists of countries of Islamic and Confucian cultures. In contrast, cluster 1 (Western) has large percentages of Protestant, Catholic, and Orthodox countries of Europe. (b) Mean AMCE z-scores of the three major clusters. Radar plot of the mean AMCE z-scores of three clusters reveals striking pattern of differences between the clusters along the nine attributes. For example, countries belonging to the Southern cluster shows strong preference for the female gender compared to those of other clusters.
